activity_context.topic_title: Row and Column Operations on Determinants

examples.knowledge_point: Calculating a Determinant After Multiplying a Matrix by a Scalar
examples.problem: Suppose $A$ is a $4\times4$ matrix and $\det(A)=5.$ What is the value of $\det(2A)?$
examples.worked_solution:
Multiplying a $n\times n$ matrix by a scalar $k$ is equivalent to multiplying each row by $k,$ and this occurs $n$ times. This leads to the result

$$
\begin{aligned}det(k\cdot A)={k}^{n}\cdot det(A).\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, we have $k=2$ and $n=4.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}det(2A) & ={2}^{4}\cdot det(A) \\  & =16\cdot 5 \\  & =80.\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem: Suppose $C$ is a $7\times 7$ matrix and $det(C)=-126.$ The matrix $D$ is obtained from $C$ by applying the elementary row operation ${R}_{5}:=\frac{8}{21}{R}_{5}.$ What is the value of $det(D)?$
feedback.worked_solution:
The row operation applied to $C$ consists of multiplying a row by the number $\frac{8}{21}.$

When we do this, the determinant is multiplied by the same number. So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}det(D) & =\frac{8}{21}det(C) \\  & =\frac{8}{21}\cdot (-126) \\  & =-48.\end{aligned}
$$
